title: refactor(driver-sql): move the upsert conflict-target path out of sql-driver.ts into sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target.ts (#25521 cut 14)

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:把 `sql-driver.ts` 里 upsert 的「冲突键预检」代码(判断表上是否真有能承接 `conflictKeys` 的唯一索引、MySQL 下是否会落到别的唯一键上,以及多组织写入的组织栅栏两个小助手)原样搬进新文件 `sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target.ts`;类上的方法全部保留,只把方法体转交过去。
- **为什么改**:#25521 拆分超大文件的第 14 刀;这块在剩余可搬区域里收益最大,`sql-driver.ts` 减少 228 行。
- **风险与回滚**:纯搬移,无行为变化;三个 SQL 驱动的测试两端逐条一致,公开类型声明哈希不变。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**:`sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target.ts` 的头注释与 host 接口;`sql-driver.ts` 中五个方法的转交桩;`refuseUnbackedConflictTarget` 上方那段文档注释如今重新紧贴它自己的函数。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run src/sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target-dialects.test.ts src/sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target-envelope.test.ts`,预期全部通过。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

Cut 14 of the `sql-driver.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`). The claim is `6431182919`. The cut opens with a fresh seam table (below), taken on `origin/main` `abb904605` (cut 13's merge), and takes the area that pays best without breaking a series limit: the **conflict-target path of `upsert`**. It moves unedited into a **new** seam module, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target.ts`, through a new host `UpsertConflictTargetHost`:

- `assertConflictTargetHonoured`, the MySQL pre-flight (#8621 unbacked, #8755 ambiguous, and #8807's identity-at-risk verdict);
- `assertConflictTargetBackedWithoutClause`, its #8740 twin for a statement with no conflict clause;
- `introspectKeyIndexes`, the cached PRIMARY KEY / UNIQUE read both consult;
- `upsertTenantGuard` and `upsertConflictRefusal`, the #21185 organization-fence helpers `driver-turso` also calls on its own instance.

The change is move-only, and the card stays open for later cuts. There is no `docs/adr/**` edit, no `packages/spec/**` edit, no anchor entry change, no test change, no gate edit and no new gate. Branch `claude/project-thread-h28rw8` (the platform assigned it to this card thread, as the claim records). The move is one commit, `84d0e45bd`, on `abb904605`.

**Net line count (the seat's rule).** `sql-driver.ts` goes from 20,022 lines to 19,794: **-228**.

- **Out:** the five bodies, 134 lines (9 + 4 + 17 + 97 + 7). Three module-level declarations that only these bodies read, 125 lines with their own docblocks plus 3 separator lines: `indexCoversConflictTarget` (11), `unbackedConflictTargetCause` (11) and `refuseAmbiguousConflictTarget` (103).
- **In:** the five stub bodies, 30 lines (6 + 2 + 7 + 8 + 7), and a 4-line import of the module with its comment.
- The new module is 359 lines.

**Why -228 and not the -320 cut 13 priced.** Two corrections, both measured on this base:

- `indexCoversConflictTarget`'s leading trivia holds two earlier comments that are not its own: the `[#8445 → #8567]` note on `isUnbackedConflictTargetError` and the `[#8445]` docblock of `refuseUnbackedConflictTarget` (80 lines; the #26015 insertion of `indexCoversConflictTarget` and `unbackedConflictTargetCause` had separated that docblock from its function). They describe code that stays, so they stay. With the two functions gone, the `[#8445]` docblock again sits directly on `refuseUnbackedConflictTarget`.
- `ConflictTargetVerdict` (15 lines) is the declared return type of the class method `assertConflictTargetHonoured`, whose signature stays in the class (and in the published `.d.ts`). It stays, exported in place.

**Serial with the file's in-flight PRs.** I read the full file list of every open PR at start (23 PRs, every page of each). Before cut 13 merged only #26377 touched `sql-driver.ts`. No other open PR touches `sql-driver.ts`, `turso-driver.ts`, `sqlite-wasm-driver.ts`, `check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` or the driver-sql anchor entries. #26138 touches `driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts` only; #26337 adds `driver-sql/src/sql-driver-external-unprovisioned-sort-anchor.test.ts` only.

### Pricing the areas

Eligibility is as cuts 11-13 defined it: an annotated return type or not public; no `getBuilder`, `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(`, private-static, `super`, bare-`this` or `this`-write site; not `insertOnlyUpsertColumns`. 129 members are eligible on this base. Each candidate area is priced as its stubs minus its bodies, then **net of the module-level declarations it shares with members that stay** (they stay in place, exported; ⛔ no second copy of a helper), counting only a declaration's own docblock.

| Area (section) | Bodies | Bodies net | Declarations that move along | Disposition |

| The rest of the Filter helpers (`compileFilters` -75, `applyNormalizedComparison` -60, …) | - | - | `filterArrayReachedDriverError` (-44) | Not priced as one area: small bodies spread around `applyFilterCondition`, which an ADR-0139 pointer pins in place. |

## Why this area

- **It pays the most of any area that moves cleanly.** The five bodies are one mechanism: what `upsert` asks of the table's physical keys before it compiles, and the fence it applies afterwards.
- **What stays, and why.**
  - `upsert` builds through `getBuilder` (2 sites) and stays, with `assertMergeLandedInWrittenOrganization`, `assertMergeLandedOnSuppliedIdentity` and `mergeLandsInWrittenOrganization`.
  - `insertOnlyUpsertColumns` stays (#8740).
  - `refuseUnbackedConflictTarget` (also thrown by `upsert`'s reactive catch), `refuseUpsertConflictOutsideWrittenOrganization` (also thrown by `upsert` and `assertMergeLandedInWrittenOrganization`) and `ConflictTargetVerdict` (the class method's return type) are shared. Each gains a leading `export` and nothing else, and the module imports them back. The module reads the two functions only inside function bodies, so the import cycle is evaluation-safe. `index.ts` names its exports one by one; the export lists below prove none of the three leaks.
  - `rotationWriteTarget`, `introspectIndexes`, `resolveTenantField` and `remoteColumn` are read by members that stay too. The moved bodies reach them through the host.
- **No series limit is touched.** None of the five builds through `getBuilder`, reads a static, has a `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site, uses `super` or a bare `this`, or writes to `this` (`introspectKeyIndexes` calls `.get`/`.set` on the `physicalKeyIndexes` map it reads through a getter, as before). Every one has an annotated return type; three are protected and two private. `check:tenant-chokepoint`'s D8 predicates, measured with its own `nullArmsOf`: **4 at base and 4 at head**, all in `sql-driver.ts`, 0 in the new module. `upsertTenantGuard` reads the tenant field to build the fence descriptor and holds no predicate; disclosed because the new module is outside the gate's `SCAN_FILES`.
- **Durability gate.** `introspectKeyIndexes` has the one `catch` in the moved code; it returns `null` and reaches no vocabulary callee. `check:durability-log-level` reads 48 seams (7 propagating) at both ends.
- **Subclasses.** `TursoDriver` calls `upsertTenantGuard` and `upsertConflictRefusal` on its own instance; both stubs keep their signatures and stay `protected`. `TursoDriver` and `SqliteWasmDriver` override none of the five. Every member the bodies call is a late-bound closure on the instance.
- **Path readers, screened.** No script, test, doc or ADR names any of the five, or the three moved declarations, by a `sql-driver.ts#…` pointer or a `sql-driver.ts::…` key. Prose mentions (`live-dialect-matrix.isolation.test.ts`, `sql-driver-introspection.ts`, `sql-driver-upsert-conflict-target-envelope.test.ts`, the turso parity tests, the driver-sql CHANGELOG) name the functions or `sql-driver.ts` as a file, and each is still true. No test reads these bodies' text by path, so no test changes.

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1-13 apply it)

- Each class method keeps its docblock and signature, byte-identical, except that the three `async` methods drop `async` (each stub returns the moved function's promise; the `.d.ts` does not carry `async`). Its body is now one host literal plus `NAME.call(host, ...)`, marked `[#25521 cut 14]`. `upsertConflictRefusal` reads no member, so its stub calls the function directly (the cut 11 shape).
- Fields go as GETTERS that read the driver at call time (`physicalTableByObject`, `physicalKeyIndexes`). Methods go as closures that call the method on the driver at call time (`introspectIndexes`, `introspectKeyIndexes`, `remoteColumn`, `resolveTenantField`, `rotationWriteTarget`). So a subclass override, an instance spy, or a field replaced after construction is still the one the body reaches (probe below).
- `UpsertConflictTargetHost` lists exactly those seven members, each typed as the class member's indexed access. There is no cast, and no member becomes public.
- **Module imports.** `StandardErrorCode` (`@objectstack/spec/api`, read by the moved `refuseAmbiguousConflictTarget`), `type DriverOptions` (`@objectstack/spec/data`), `type PhysicalIndex` (`./schema-drift.js`), and from `./sql-driver.js` the three shared declarations plus `type SqlDriver`. No `sql-driver.ts` import lost its last reader.
- **Comments.** The module header says what moved, what stayed and why. The `sql-driver.ts` import comment names cut 14 in 3 lines. The header cites no `ADR-NNNN Dn`.
- **How the move was made.** A script produced it from the source text; nothing was retyped. Each body line is re-indented two columns; no body line starts inside a template literal.

## ADR anchors

- **The count.** `check:adr-anchors` counts **1877** decision-letter citations at base `abb904605` (a clean detached worktree) and **1877** at head, over 91 anchored files at both ends. Both runs exit 0.
- **Why equal.** No comment inside the moved bodies or declarations cites a decision letter. The one `ADR-0120 D1` near this code is in `upsertTenantGuard`'s docblock, which stays on the class method.
- **No entry needs a new home.** The `sql-driver.ts` entry's one paragraph (ADR-0053) describes `formatOutput` and `presentReadValue`, neither of which moved. No `scripts/adr-anchors/**` file changed.

## The published `.d.ts` does not change

This is measured under the series bar (ruling `6348891160`, item 1).

- **How each end was built.** `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/driver-sql --force` at each end, against the same dependency tree. The base leg writes base `sql-driver.ts` into this worktree and deletes the new module, under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap that restores HEAD. The restore is proved by the HEAD blob hashes (`25041557`, `bcb95569`), an empty `git diff HEAD` and 0 status entries.
- **The hashes.** The raw sha256 of `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` is the same at base and at head, `0f33bf3febaac3c7aa96f68a4226d752766b8203ab7acade523b69f9aaa44d74` (unchanged since cut 8).
- **Positive control.** I dropped `protected` from `assertConflictTargetHonoured` in the head `index.d.ts`. The result hashes to `0f7f0de877d0becf5acec215a618fa3922518b60690f91898bec355659e1e21a`, with a 1-line diff and `cmp` exit 1.
- **Export lists.** CJS `require` of the head dist gives 59 names, the same set as its ESM `import` (sha1 `05757ce5ae`); the ESM export statement of the base and head `index.mjs` lists the same 59 names (sha1 `05757ce5ae` both). None of the three newly exported declarations, and nothing from the new module, is among them.
- **The head dist carries the move.** `.call(host` sites in `index.mjs` go from 47 at base to 51 at head (four stubs; the fifth calls directly).

## Move-only proof

The proof compares TypeScript compiler AST leaf tokens (JSDoc nodes skipped), base `abb904605` against head `84d0e45bd`. It is a scratch script and is not committed.

| Moved body | Body tokens | Comments | Parameter tokens less `this` | Return type tokens | Body lines |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `upsertTenantGuard` | 89 | 2 | 15 | 15 | 9 |
| `upsertConflictRefusal` | 23 | 0 | 9 | 1 | 4 |
| `introspectKeyIndexes` | 111 | 2 | 15 | 8 | 17 |
| `assertConflictTargetHonoured` | 423 | 54 | 11 | 4 | 97 |
| `assertConflictTargetBackedWithoutClause` | 114 | 0 | 11 | 4 | 7 |

- **Each moved body.** In every row, 0 tokens differ and every comment is identical. Each body line is the base line less two leading spaces. `async` matches the base method on all five functions.
- **The five stubs.** Leading trivia (the docblock), modifiers and the signature are identical to base, less `async` on the three async methods.
- **The class.** It has 350 members at both ends, in the same order, and the 345 unmoved members are byte-identical, trivia included.
- **Module-level declarations.** The three that moved are byte-identical in the module from their own docblock on, and gone from `sql-driver.ts`. The three shared ones differ from base by a leading `export` and nothing else. `refuseUnbackedConflictTarget`'s leading trivia is now exactly the 80 lines of earlier comments that stayed from `indexCoversConflictTarget`'s trivia (checked byte for byte). At `sql-driver.ts`'s top level, 194 of 201 base statements are byte-identical. The rest are the three moved declarations, the three exports and the class; the one head-only statement besides those is the new import.
- **Result.** `PROOF OK`, exit 0.
- **Negative control.** Through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, I changed `introspectKeyIndexes(tableName, { fresh: true })` to `{ fresh: false }` in the module (1 hit, checked on disk). The proof then reports `assertConflictTargetHonoured` with its body tokens differing, prints `PROOF FAILED`, and exits 1. The restore was proved (blob equals HEAD, empty `git diff HEAD`).

## Tests

Each end ran under one `os-verify-lock` hold, after building that end's driver-sql dist. I compared the vitest JSON per test name and status, base `abb904605` against head `84d0e45bd`. Every part's exit code was captured on its own (build, probe, three suites: all 0 at both ends).

| Suite | Base | Head | Lost / changed / added |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/driver-sql` | 4060 (3846 passed, 214 skipped; 248 files) | same | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `@objectstack/driver-turso`, against that end's built driver-sql dist | 2526 (2492 passed, 34 skipped; 95 files) | same | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` | 746 (746 passed; 39 files) | same | 0 / 0 / 0 |

- **Type check and lint.** `tsc --noEmit -p .` in driver-sql exits 0. `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config packages/drivers/driver-sql` exits 0.
- **Late-binding probe.** A scratch script, not committed. It runs node against each end's built dist on in-memory SQLite and prints 50 readings:
  1. `upsertTenantGuard` on six rows (no options, empty `tenantId`, the tenant row, another organization's row, a row without the value, a non-tenant object) and `upsertConflictRefusal` on one, two, empty and absent keys, with instance spies on all five host methods showing the calls in order;
  2. `introspectKeyIndexes` cold, cached, `fresh`, on a keyless table and a missing one, with `introspectIndexes` replaced on the instance by a throwing read (`null`), and with the `physicalKeyIndexes` map replaced on the instance after construction (the new map is the one read);
  3. `assertConflictTargetHonoured` on every verdict: ambiguous named and unnamed, identity at risk (`id` with rivals) on two tables, honoured, unbacked named and unnamed, a composite unbacked target, a missing table, and a stale cache re-read before a refusal;
  4. `assertConflictTargetBackedWithoutClause` backed, unbacked, on `id`, and on a missing table;
  5. a SUBCLASS overriding `rotationWriteTarget`, `resolveTenantField`, `remoteColumn` and `introspectIndexes`, each reached, and `physicalTableByObject` shadowed on the instance after construction (the refusal's `cause` names the shadowed table);
  6. nine `upsert()`/`find()` calls end to end on SQLite: a seed and a merge, two unbacked refusals through the reactive catch (one tenant-scoped), and tenant-scoped composite upserts in two organizations, read back;
  7. bad arguments on four of the methods.
- **Probe result.** 49 of the 50 readings are identical, refusal `code`, `status`, message and `cause` included. The other one is the bad-argument row of `upsertTenantGuard`: it throws the same `TypeError` with the same message, and only the top stack frame's receiver name differs, `_SqlDriver.upsertTenantGuard` at base and `Object.upsertTenantGuard` at head. That is the host-literal receiver of shape B, the same at every earlier cut, and no test or consumer reads it.
- **Not run.** No ablation, because no tested behaviour changed.
- **`test:repo`.** The `repo` projects of types (11), core (83), objectql (5), spec (1279) and rest (280 passed, 18 skipped) pass locally after building rest's closure. Runtime's is NOT MEASURED locally; CI's Test Core runs all of them.
- **After the merge of `origin/main`** (`8adeb4ba47`, 11 commits, no `packages/drivers/**` file): `tsc` exits 0, the two upsert conflict-target test files pass (22 passed, 3 skipped), and `check:adr-anchors` still reads 1877.

## Acceptance notes

- **`check:tenant-chokepoint`'s D8 rule does not scan the new module.** The moved bodies hold 0 of the file's 4 tenant predicates (measured with the gate's own `nullArmsOf`), and none builds a query. Noted, not filed: widening `SCAN_FILES` would be a gate change.
- **A docblock returns to its function.** The `[#8445]` docblock of `refuseUnbackedConflictTarget` had been separated from it by the two helpers #26015 inserted; with them moved it again sits on its function. Its bytes are unchanged, and the published `.d.ts` does not carry it (the function is not exported from `index.ts`).
- **Next slice, priced on this base.** The backend statement fault classifier (`backendStatementFault` with `backendStatementFaultError`) pays about -216; it reads `logger`, so it needs a `check:logger-receiver-detach` and `check:durability-log-level` screen first.
